answer: Original papers in Experimental Economics (project='ee') average about 28.0 pages (n=18), whereas original papers in Psychology (project='rpp') average about 11.2 pages (n=97) — EE originals are roughly 2.5× longer. Page counts are from the 'length' column, which the schema defines as the number of pages of the original paper. The ee figure rests on a small sample (18 papers, range 16–45 pages), so it should be read as approximate rather than precise; the rpp estimate (97 papers, range 1–31 pages) is more stable.

payload.hypothesis: Original papers in the Experimental Economics replication project (ee) are substantially longer than those in the Psychology project (rpp): ee originals average 28.0 pages (n=18) versus 11.2 pages for rpp originals (n=97), i.e., roughly 2.5× longer. Length is measured in pages per the schema ('length' = number of pages of original paper).
payload.workflow: Loaded the 927-row meta-regression study data CSV with pandas. Filtered to project=='ee' (18 rows) and project=='rpp' (97 rows). Verified 'length' (pages of original paper, per schema) is fully numeric with 0 missing, 0 zero/negative, and max 45 — no invalid values, so no rows were excluded. Computed the per-row arithmetic mean of 'length' per project: ee = 28.00 (n=18), rpp = 11.22 (n=97), ratio 2.50. Computed sensitivity excluding drop=True rows (rpp: 11.00, n=90; ee unaffected, no drop=True rows) and a per-unique-paper robustness variant (rpp: 11.23, n=95; ee unchanged). The second dataset was not used (it has no length column).
